Hi team,

Looping everyone in for the implementation kickoff next week. Finlytics has shared a concise traffic snapshot and a short list of model preferences; I've attached their token profile CSV and the POC requirements workbook. Key points from discovery that we should act on before the kickoff: 

- Primary use case: real-time summary + follow-up suggestion for finance reconciliation cases (average user session ~3 exchanges).
- Peak concurrency: they expect up to 40 concurrent users during billing cycle runs (spike ~2 hours/day).
- Per-request context window: up to 2.5k tokens (includes recent conversation + 2 doc references).
- Monthly token volume (estimate from Claire): 22M tokens/month (growth to 45M in Q2).

Requesting action items: 
1) Ben — can you prepare a quick model shortlist (3 variants) with rationale (latency vs cost vs quality) and recommended initial quantization level for the initial Dedicated pool? Please include expected throughput per GPU for their average/session profile.
2) Monica — please draft a minimal mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones we can present at kickoff (integration, security review, Prod API key swap).
3) Claire — thanks for the CSV; can you confirm the 22M number is monthly total (inference + context) and whether system prompts are sent on every request?

Goal: have Ben's shortlist and Monica's MAP by EOD Friday (2026-12-11) so we can circulate ahead of the kickoff on Monday.

Thanks,
Aisha

Thanks Aisha — quick pass from my side. I reviewed the token profile and the session characteristics. My initial shortlist (three options) below with pros/cons and rough per-GPU throughput assumptions for our Dedicated v2 (A100-like) profile when serving with continuous batching and prefix caching: 

1) Model A (open-llama-13B-opt) — Latency: low/medium; Cost: low; Quality: good for summarization tasks.
   - Throughput: ~650 tokens/s per GPU
   - Notes: handles 2.5k context comfortably when quantized to 4-bit; good cost savings for 22M/month.

2) Model B (redwood-inc-slim-20B) — Latency: medium; Cost: medium; Quality: higher on finance-specific terminology.
   - Throughput: ~420 tokens/s per GPU
   - Notes: recommend FP16 or 8-bit fallback; better for edge-case accuracy and more robust on multi-doc prompts.

3) Model C (redwood-chat-7B-qlora) — Latency: very low; Cost: very low; Quality: reasonable for short-answer follow-ups.
   - Throughput: ~900 tokens/s per GPU
   - Notes: best as a fallback / low-cost tier for non-critical suggestions; may fail softer on complex reconciliation language.

Recommendations: start with a dual-variant strategy: primary = Model B (for quality-critical flows during weekdays), fallback = Model C for burst traffic and cheaper night/weekend processing. Use Model A as a mid-tier for gradual cost tuning. Initial quantization: Model B at FP16 for the first 2 weeks of POC to avoid regressions, then evaluate 8-bit/4-bit profiling.

Capacity estimate for 22M tokens/month:
- If we assume 60% generation, 40% prompt/context tokens (their CSV shows ~1.8k tokens per full request on average), expected sustained throughput: ~8.7M generation tokens/month.
- With Model B at 420 tokens/s per GPU, a single GPU translates to ~36M tokens/month (theoretical), but accounting for batching inefficiencies and multi-tenant overhead, plan for 0.6x => ~21.6M tokens/month per GPU.
- So initial Dedicated commitment: 1 GPU with autoscale + 1 spare for failover during peak windows, and a burst policy to add 1-2 GPUs for the 2-hour daily peak.

I'll prepare a one-pager with the numbers and expected latency/cost tradeoffs for the kickoff deck. Will also include quick benchmark notes for quantization options.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aisha, Ben — quick clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: 22M tokens/month includes both prompt (context + user) and generation tokens; system prompts are appended on ~95% of requests (we keep a short company policy prompt).
- Typical session pattern: opener (250 tokens) + 2 follow-ups (avg 375 tokens each) + system prompt ~120 tokens when included. That aligns with your 1.8k/request average.
- Peak concurrency: 40 concurrent live users, but about 120 total active API keys generating requests during the daily 2-hour window.
- Attachments: Uploaded a sanitized sample conversation log to the Drive folder (not sending PII). Link in the Drive folder.

We are comfortable starting on the FP16 path for Model B as long as you can provide a short QA checklist for hallucination / numeric fidelity checks. For the MAP, please include a sandbox validation step and a short rollback policy if we see >2% regression in reconciliation accuracy on the QA set.

Claire
